message.content:
The coordinator sent a message while you were working:
Round 7: please review the redesigned trail_report.go. After /simplify I changed the approach instead of adding more rules. Re-run all your earlier probes against the current tree (some need updating, because ListItemText and StartsWithSeverityMarker are now unexported as listItemText and startsWithSeverityMarker, and severityGroupLabel and severityLabel now return a string). Then hunt for new defects. Same rules: realistic inputs only, verify each with go test -overlay, and never write to the repo.

The new design:
- Completeness (comments non-empty): markedLineCount(prose) <= len(comments) AND locationsCovered(prose, comments). markedLineCount counts lines at any indentation, unwrapped from list items, that open with a severity marker, skipping severity group labels. locationsCovered requires every file:line cited in the prose (LocationPattern) to fall inside the location range of some comment on the same path (suffix match), or to appear in a comment's body.
- Clean check (comments []): the prose reports findings if it has a non-placeholder list item at any indentation, any file:line, or anything proseReportsMarkedFindings finds (a marker line other than a group label, a feedback label, or a non-approving verdict).
- Borrowing for a JSON-only final message: textStretches splits the buffer once in a linear pass, and the review borrows the latest earlier stretch for which proseReportsMarkedFindings is true. It deliberately ignores locations, so narration like "Let me read retry.go:40" is not borrowed.
- SplitProseFindings now only shapes how fallback prose is posted. No posting decision uses it. A sub-heading in a group holds everything up to the next heading; merging a sub-heading's bullets into one finding is intended and fine. Detail labels, bold-paragraph splitting and title rules are gone.
- The JSON instruction now also asks for one comment per finding however the prose is laid out, and for every cited file:line to fall in some comment's location.

The bar has changed to fit the design. Report a defect only if a realistic output: (a) loses a real finding, meaning it is never posted anywhere, (b) posts a clean review, or (c) is a clear code-quality problem in the new code. When an accurate contract loses to prose that cites an extra evidence location, that is accepted fail-open behavior, not a defect, so mention it only as minor. Cosmetic splitting or merging of fallback prose is minor. Say "no findings" plainly if there are none, and list minor items separately.

Address this before completing your current task.

The redesign still has 2 qualifying defects. One loses real findings (a). The other posts clean reviews (b), and it is new in this round. Both were checked with `go test -overlay` probes; the new one is `.../scratchpad/agent/probe5_test.go`. No repo files were written. I found no code-quality problems (c).

**Re-run of earlier probes (P, N, R, S and all bridge probes; `markedFindingCount` renamed to `markedLineCount` in my copy):**
- All clean reviews give `post=false`: P1, P1b, N4, N4b, N6.
- Accurate contracts win in N1b, N2, N3, N7 and S1 to S4.
- The bridge output shapes are fine.
- R1 now loses a finding; see defect 1.

**1. Loss: unmarked findings under a severity heading are no longer counted, so a short contract wins when the extra finding has no file:line.** `trail_report.go:100-108` (`contractCoversProse`, `markedLineCount`).
- **Cause:** `markedLineCount` skips the `### High` label and counts only lines that open with a severity marker. A bullet under a severity heading counts for nothing, so `locationsCovered` is the only check left. A finding cited by anything except `file.ext:N` passes it.
- **Shared contract for every input below:** `{"summary":"one issue","comments":[{"severity":"high","body":"Unbounded retry loop never stops on 503; cap attempts.","location":{"granularity":"line","file_path":"internal/retry.go","start_line":42}}]}`
- **Inputs, all observed `post=true comments=1 prose=""`:**
  - "line N" style: `"### High
- `retry.go:42`: the retry loop never stops on 503.
- `retry.go` line 80: the error from `Close` is swallowed.

### Low
None."`
  - GitHub anchors: `"### High
- `retry.go#L42`: …
- `auth.go#L10`: the bearer token is logged.

### Low
None."`
  - File or function name only: `"### High
- `retry.go:42`: …
- `Client.Do` in `auth.go` logs the bearer token at info level.

### Low
None."`
  - Old R1: `"## High

### `retry.go`
- Line 42: …
- Line 80: the error from `Close` is swallowed."`
- **Expected:** the prose is posted, because the second finding is in no comment. Base `edb58891a` and rounds 4 to 6 all posted the prose here.
- **Fix:** add a third signal that holds for the common shape. Count the top-level, non-placeholder list items that sit directly under a severity group label, outside any deeper sub-heading. Require `len(comments) >=` that count as well. Detail bullets under a sub-heading stay uncounted, so S1 to S4 keep the contract.
- **Optional:** widen `LocationPattern` to also catch `file#L80` and "`file` line 80".

**2. Clean review posted: any file:line in approving prose contradicts `comments:[]`.** `trail_report.go:317` (`proseReportsFindings`: `LocationPattern.MatchString(prose) || …`).
- **Input:** `"## Summary

The new backoff in `retry.go:42` correctly caps attempts at 5, and `retry_test.go:88` covers the 503 path.

### High
None.

### Medium
None.

### Low
None.

**Verdict:** Approve"` plus `{"summary":"Looks good.","comments":[]}`
- **Observed:** `post=true`, and the whole approval is posted as prose.
- **Expected:** `post=false`.
- **Why it matters:** reviewers routinely cite file:line as evidence in an approval.
- **Fix:** don't use a bare file:line as a clean-check signal. If you keep it, count a location only when it sits in a list item or inside a severity group, not in summary or verdict paragraphs.

**Minor:**
- **Checklist bullets in a clean review still post it.** Input: `"## Summary

What I checked:
- The retry cap is enforced on every path.
- Tests cover the 503 case.

No issues found.

**Verdict:** Approve"` plus `comments:[]` gives `post=true`. This list-item rule predates this diff, but it meets bar (b) if you want to tighten it. One option: ignore list items that come after a "What I checked/Verified" lead-in, or when the prose has an approving verdict and a no-issues placeholder.
- **An unmarked report before a JSON-only final line is not borrowed.** Events: `"## Findings

1. `retry.go:42` — the retry loop never stops on 503.

  - `Nothing to add.`

The structural fix from defect 1 covers these too: a single sentence opening with none/nothing/no, with no contrastive word and no code or file reference, is a placeholder. There are 2 qualifying defects: a crash (c) and a finding-loss regression (a), both in the new `isNoFindingsText`. Both were checked with `go test -overlay` (new probe: `.../scratchpad/agent/probe8_test.go`). No repo files were written.

**Re-run of all earlier probes (P, N, R, S, probe5, probe6, probe7 and all bridge probes):**
- **Clean reviews, `post=false`:** P1/P1b, N4/N4b/N6, C1, all 8 round-8 placeholders plus `_None._`, and 7 of the 8 round-9 placeholders. The eighth, `Clean.`, still posts, which is acceptable fail-open.
- **Findings posted:** F1 to F4 and the F5 "None of" control all post the prose.
- **Earlier losses now post the prose:** L1/L1b/L2, R1/R3, and both cases without line numbers.
- **Accepted:** the fail-open contract cases, C2 and B1, unchanged.
- **Bridge:** same shapes as before.

**1. Crash (c): an em or en dash as a placeholder panics.** `trail_report.go:554` (`switch words[0]`).
- **Cause:** "—" survives the end trim. The `strings.Map` step then turns it into a space, so `words` is empty and `words[0]` is out of range.
- **Inputs:**
  - `"### High\n—\n\n### Medium\n—\n\n### Low\n—\n\n**Verdict:** Approve"` + `{"summary":"Looks good.","comments":[]}`
  - `"### High\n–\n\n### Low\n–"` + the same contract.
- **Observed:** `trailReportFor` panics with `runtime error: index out of range [0] with length 0`.
- **Reach:**
  - `scanSeverityGroups` calls it on a group's first content.
  - `proseReportsFindings` calls it on any list item, so `- —` crashes too.
  - SplitProseFindings and the bridge do as well.
  - A dash is a common "empty" marker, so this would crash `entire review --output trail`.
- **Expected:** the dash is treated as a placeholder, so `post=false`.
- **Fix:** `if len(words) == 0 { return true }`. The text is only punctuation or dashes, which is an empty-section marker. Also drop the now-unreachable `"-"` case, or keep it consistent with this.

**2. Regression (a): a finding that opens with "No …" and mentions a finding noun anywhere is taken as a placeholder.** `trail_report.go:561-566` (the `case "no"` branch scans every later word for a noun).
- **Shared frame for the contract cases:** `"### High\n- `retry.go:42`: the retry loop never stops on 503.\n\n### Medium\n<X>\n\n### Low\nNone."` + one comment at retry.go:42.
- **With that contract, observed `post=true comments=1` (the Medium finding is never posted):**
  - `<X>` = `No test covers the 503 path in the auth client, so regressions there would go unnoticed.`
  - `<X>` = `- No cap on the token refresh loop, which risks hammering the auth server.`
- **With `comments:[]`, observed `post=false` (the only finding is never posted):**
  - `"### Medium\n- No test covers the 503 path, so this bug class could come back unnoticed.\n\n### Low\nNone."`
  - `"### High\nNo timeout on the HTTP client in the auth flow, a real availability risk under load.\n\n### Low\nNone."`
- **Expected:** the prose is posted in every case.
- **Why it matters:** "No <missing thing> …, which risks / so regressions …" is one of the most common ways LLM reviewers phrase a finding.
- **Fix:** require the noun to be what "no" negates, within at most about 3 words ("No issues", "No high-severity issues", "No new blocking concerns"). After it, allow only a short tail such as found, identified, noted, introduced, to report, here, or in/at this change/severity/diff. In practice, reject any text where a word after "no" and before the noun is outside a small modifier set, or where a comma clause or a verb such as covers, is, could or risks follows. A simpler and still fail-open variant is to accept "no" only when the noun is among `words[1:4]` and there is no comma in `s`.

No other new defects.

All earlier probes pass, but the placeholder rule still has one qualifying defect: findings phrased "No regression test…" or "Nothing to/here …" are read as an empty section and never posted (a). It was checked with `go test -overlay` (new probe: `.../scratchpad/agent/probe9_test.go`). No repo files were written. No crash or other code-quality issue (c).

**Re-run of all earlier probes (P, N, R, S, probe5 to probe8 and the three bridge probes):**
- **Round-10 fixes hold:** D1/D2 (a bare em or en dash) are placeholders with no panic, and G1 to G4 post the prose.
- **Clean reviews, `post=false`:** P1/P1b, N4/N4b/N6, C1, all round-8 and round-9 placeholders, and the em/en dash cases.
- **Findings posted:** F1 to F5, L1/L1b/L2, R1/R3, and both cases without line numbers.
- **Accepted:** the contract-loses cases, C2, B1 and "Clean.", unchanged.
- **Bridge:** all three probes run (6, 4 and 2 findings, the same shapes as before).

**Defect (a): a "No …" or "Nothing …" finding whose noun or qualifier comes early is still read as a placeholder.** `trail_report.go:559-576` (`isNoFindingsText`).
- **Why:** "No regression test …": "regression" is in `findingNouns` and sits in `words[1:4]`, and there is no comma, so the sentence reads as "no regressions". Likewise `nothingQualifiers` admits "to" and "here" whatever follows.
- **Case 1 (realistic, very common missing-test finding):** `"### High\nNone.\n\n### Medium\n- No regression test covers the new 503 retry cap\n\n### Low\nNone."` + `{"summary":"Looks good.","comments":[]}`
  - Observed: `post=false`, so the only finding is never posted.
- **Case 2:** `"### High\n- `retry.go:42`: the retry loop never stops on 503.\n\n### Medium\nNo regression tests were added for the token redaction in the auth client\n\n### Low\nNone."` + one comment at retry.go:42.
  - Observed: `post=true comments=1`, so the Medium finding is lost.
- **Case 3 (less common phrasing, same mechanism):** `"### High\nNothing to stop the retry loop from spinning forever when the server keeps returning 503\n\n### Low\nNone."` + `comments:[]`.
  - Observed: `post=false`.
- **Case 4 (same mechanism):** `"### Medium\nNothing here handles the 503 case in the auth client\n\n### Low\nNone."` + `comments:[]`.
  - Observed: `post=false`.
- **Expected in all four:** the prose is posted.
- **Fix:** constrain what may follow the qualifier as well as what precedes it.
  - **"no" branch:** after the noun, allow only end of text or a closed tail set: found, identified, noted, introduced, to report, here, and in/at/for followed by this/the and change/diff/pr/severity/level/area/section. Then "No regression test covers…" fails, because "test" follows the noun. "No regressions found" and "No issues at this severity" still pass.
  - **"nothing" branch:** accept "to" only before flag, report, note, add or mention. Accept "here" only at the end. Treat "new", "worth" and the others the same way: the qualifier must end the text or be followed by a tail word.

No other new defects.

  - `No issues in this category.`
  - `No issues identified in this review.`
  - `No concerns from me.`

It was checked with `go test -overlay` (new probe: `.../scratchpad/agent/probe11_test.go`). No repo files were written. No crash or code-quality issue (c).

**Re-run of all earlier probes (P, N, R, S, probe5 to probe10, and the three bridge probes):** everything is correct and unchanged.
- **Clean reviews give `post=false`:** P1/P1b, N4/N4b/N6, C1, every placeholder from rounds 8 to 11 (including all 10 in probe10), `_None._`, and the em and en dash.
- **Findings post the prose:** F1 to F5, G1 to G4, H1 to H4, L1/L1b/L2, R1/R3, and the cases without line numbers.
- **Accepted:** C2, B1, "Clean.", "None — <finding>" and the contract-loses cases are unchanged.
- **Bridge:** same shapes (6, 4 and 2 findings).

**Defect (a): a "No <thing> <verb> … <noun>" finding is read as a placeholder.** `trail_report.go`, `isNoFindingsText`, "no" branch.
- **Why:** the finding noun is found within `words[1:5]`, and everything before it is treated as a free modifier, including the verb and determiner. Nothing follows the noun, so the line counts as an empty section.
- **Inputs:**
  - `"### High\nNone.\n\n### Medium\nNo test covers this regression.\n\n### Low\nNone."` + `{"summary":"Looks good.","comments":[]}`
    - Observed: `post=false`, so the only finding is never posted.
  - The same line under `### Medium` after `"### High\n- `retry.go:42`: the retry loop never stops on 503.\n\n"`, with one comment at retry.go:42.
    - Observed: `post=true comments=1`, so the Medium finding is lost.
  - `- No tests cover the regression`, in both frames: same results (`post=false`, and `comments=1`).
- **Controls that correctly post:** `- No test for the regression this change fixes` and `No test covers the fixed bug.`
- **Expected:** the prose is posted.
- **Before:** the round-11 version (noun among `words[1:4]`) rejected "No test covers this regression"? No. It also accepted it; but the round-12 version made the modifiers free, so this is the shape to close now.
- **Fix:** constrain the free modifiers. Allow at most 2, and reject the text if any modifier is a determiner or preposition (the, this, these, that, a, an, for, of, in, on, to) or a verb in third person or plural (cover, covers, handle, handles, check, checks).
  - Still placeholders: "No security concerns", "No correctness or security issues", "No obvious issues" and "No high-severity issues".
  - Rejected as findings: "No test covers this regression" and "No tests cover the regression".
  - A simpler variant is to reject when any modifier is a determiner or preposition. Real placeholders never put one between "no" and the noun.

No other new defects.
